A common path is an engineering bachelor's degree, a master's or doctorate, a postdoctoral or lecturer role, parallel growth in teaching and research, promotion from lecturer to associate professor to professor, and continued industry collaboration.

This role suits people who can explain ideas clearly and build things in practice. If you can turn Maxwell's equations into a compelling explanation and spend hours helping students tune equipment, the classroom and lab can be your arena.

Engineering Teachers, Postsecondary teach civil, mechanical, electrical, computing, and other engineering subjects at universities and technical colleges. They guide laboratories, internships, and capstone projects and conduct research, technology development, and industry-academic collaboration. They connect engineering education with industry practice.

paragraphs: A score of 5/10 indicates moderate exposure. AI takes over much of the desk work in teaching, including slides, grading, and literature review. Faculty value shifts toward classroom interaction, laboratory guidance, and research judgment.

Moderate exposure does not mean high job risk. AI replaces teaching that simply reads from slides, not faculty who know how to teach. The divide will widen: faculty who use AI tools can become far more productive, while those who retain old methods face increasing difficulty.

Plan for the long investment in a doctorate and publications before choosing this path. Emerging engineering fields such as AI, new energy, and semiconductors have larger faculty shortages. Career and technical education also offers opportunities.

Bring AI tools into teaching. Use them for slides, question banks, and grading, then invest the saved time in laboratory guidance and individualized coaching. Industry-academic projects can provide income and useful course material.

Engineers seeking faculty roles should add teaching experience through assistantships, laboratories, or online courses. Avoid positions with extreme up-or-out pressure. Career colleges and emerging engineering schools often need more faculty.

Do not hire engineering faculty by publication count alone. Require a teaching demonstration, review course design, and examine student feedback. Faculty who integrate AI tools and connect with industry merit stronger appointments and startup support.

This role suits people who enjoy making complex ideas simple and care about student development.

The most rewarding part of this work is influencing people. A student who once thought programming was impossible can understand after a clear explanation. Former graduate students can later join leading companies or universities. That achievement can matter more than another paper.

If you enjoy helping students move from not understanding to applying a concept well, and you have the patience for sustained research, engineering teaching deserves serious consideration.
